aiOverview.content: Based on recent reports, former FBI Director and Special Counsel Robert Mueller was subpoenaed by the House Oversight Committee in August 2025 regarding the Justice Department's handling of the Jeffrey Epstein case, but the subpoena was withdrawn due to his health, specifically a Parkinson's disease diagnosis. Key Details Regarding Mueller and the Epstein Investigation: Subpoena and Withdrawal: Rep. James Comer, chairman of the House Oversight Committee, issued the subpoena to testify regarding the long-term investigation into Epstein. The committee withdrew it after learning of Mueller's health issues. Parkinson's Diagnosis: Mueller’s family disclosed in August 2025 that he was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the summer of 2021. Context of Investigation: The investigation focused on the 2008 non-prosecution agreement that allowed Epstein to plead guilty to state charges in Florida. Mueller was the FBI director at that time (2001–2013). Epstein File Mentions: In documents related to Epstein released by the DOJ, Mueller's name appeared in communications from 2017 to 2018 where Epstein discussed the Russia probe with associates. Note: Robert Mueller died on March 21, 2026, at the age of 81.
